newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy vows significant arms cuts to update treaty.
newsitem.headline: Italy vows significant arms cuts to update treaty.

text.p: Italy plans "significant" cuts in the number of heavy weapons it can legally own to speed progress towards updating a 1990 European arms treaty, a foreign ministry source said on Thursday.

Earlier France offered to cut its own stocks of armaments as negotiators in Austria seek to rewrite the Conventional Forces in Europe (CFE) treaty, which imposes ceilings on the amount of weaponry any country can hold.

Italy will "voluntarily" reduce its number of tanks, armoured vehicles, artillery and combat aircraft by six percent compared with current CFE ceilings for specific weapon groups, the foreign ministry source said.
"Italy hopes that such a significant reduction on its future national (arms) ceiling will help...bring about a swifter conclusion to the negotiations on the treaty."

The seven-year-old CFE treaty is one of the key post-Cold War accords limiting numbers of weapons and where they can be placed. NATO wants to scrap group ceilings in favour of purely national ceilings while Russia wants to retain them.
Diplomats are working on the new treaty in Vienna. Italy hopes an agreement can be reached before the end of the current negotiating session on July 25.
